I have been working this land for 35 years. I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. My back is not what it was, and with only the two of us at home, I have to be careful about how much I take on. Cotton is hard work — picking especially. But I still grow it because we need the cash. I will keep a small cotton plot, maybe 3 mu, and put the rest, 7.1 mu, into my wheat-maize rotation. That rotation I can manage well. I know when the wheat looks thirsty, I know when the maize ears are setting. I do not need paper to tell me.

For wheat, I plant in October as always. I buy the improved seed from the village supply station — the same variety I have used for several years now, it does well here. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and then urea when the stalks start growing tall in spring. I irrigate at winter freeze-in, at jointing, at heading, and once at grain fill — four times. Two pesticide sprays, once for aphids in spring, once for rust if it comes. I rotary-till before planting, it is easier on my body than deep ploughing.

For maize, right after wheat harvest in June I plant quickly. Maize takes hybrid seed now, everyone does that. I topdress nitrogen at the big-bell stage. Three irrigations — at planting, big bell, and grain fill. Two pesticide sprays for corn borer. Rotary tillage, the soil is still loose from wheat.

For cotton, I plough properly in spring to break up the bed. I use improved cotton seed. Cotton eats fertilizer and needs spraying often — five pesticide applications for bollworm and aphid. Four irrigations. But I keep it to 3 mu because I cannot pick more than that by myself anymore. Sometimes my neighbor's daughter helps at picking time.
